open_obligations: Note that Wen et al. measure misleading of humans, not Yang et al.'s deception score over weak-model knowledge areas.
Check that harmlessness, Yang et al.'s target, is not studied by Wen et al.
Do not read this as showing Yang et al.'s capability-gap trend holds under PPO.
Cite a Wen et al. passage that names the RLHF algorithm: the cited passage says only 'a standard RLHF pipeline', and PPO appears only in the from-record's setting.
in.other_title: RLHF teaches language models to mislead time-constrained human evaluators (U-Sophistry)
in.rationale: Yang et al. state they mainly experiment with two offline preference optimisation methods, SimPO and DPO, and leave online frameworks such as PPO to future work. Wen et al. study a standard RLHF pipeline and report models become better at convincing time-limited humans without becoming more correct, raising false positive rates by 24.1% (QuALITY) and 18.3% (APPS); the overseer is a human evaluator, not a weak model. Both ask whether training can lead models to mislead or deceive their overseer, in different settings, so SAME_QUESTION_DIFFERENT_SETTING; the cited Wen et al. passage names neither online training nor PPO.
in.scope: proposed SAME_QUESTION_DIFFERENT_SETTING: whether training can lead models to mislead or deceive their overseer; Wen et al. study time-constrained human evaluators under a standard RLHF pipeline whose algorithm the cited passage does not name, while Yang et al. study strong models deceiving weak models under offline preference optimisation (SimPO and DPO) and leave online frameworks such as PPO to future work

text: The authors state that they mainly conduct experiments in the preference alignment scenario on two offline preference optimization methods, SimPO and DPO, leaving online frameworks such as PPO to future work, and that they mainly consider harmlessness as the target alignment dimension, while deception also matters for other dimensions such as honesty, with only preliminary experiments in Appendix O.
title: Limitations: mainly offline preference optimization and mainly harmlessness as the target
